summary.text: Bruce Starr is a Republican member of the Oregon State Senate for District 12, which his legislative page lists as rural Polk and Yamhill Counties.
His biography says he served in the Oregon House and Senate from 1999 to 2014 and later returned to the Senate after being elected from District 12.

paragraphs.text: Senator Starr grew up on a farm in Hillsboro, according to his biography, and graduated from Hillsboro High School.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Portland State University and worked as a legislative intern in the state senate while in college.

His biography says he began in public service with Washington County's Republican Central Committee, as a Hillsboro precinct committee person and on the Hillsboro City Council before moving on to the State House and Senate.

When he was first elected to the Senate in 2002, he and his father, Charles Starr, who served a neighboring district, became the first father and son to serve together in the Oregon legislature, the page says.

He chaired the House Business and Transportation Committee, served as vice chair of the Senate's transportation committee, and the page calls him instrumental in the 1999 passage of the Oregon Transportation Investment Act and lists the 2009 passage of the Jobs and Transportation Act among his proudest achievements.
In the private sector, Starr has operated small businesses ranging from political consulting to fence contracting and co-founded a Christian preschool.
He and his wife, Rebecca, moved to Dundee in 2020, where he served on the Dundee City Council until he was elected to the Senate, and they have two adult children.
